title: Ops playbook — PM/Eng sync prep (Hannah Lin)
content:
Context / purpose:
Quick prep notes for my recurring alignment session with Marcus (eng lead) — primary focus: API/Console rollout readiness for next Dedicated capacity wave + Private onboarding checklist. Half tactical, half decision record so we can close open action items by EOW. Keep this close to the meeting and paste follow-ups into the Slack thread afterwards.

High-level goals for the sync:
- Agree on final gating checklist for Dedicated wave 6 (SLOs, canary plan, autoscaling thresholds).
- Reconfirm Private deployment onboarding steps and estimate single-customer lead time.
- Decide whether to flip caching KV persistence on by default for hosted tier (risk vs unit-cost win).
- Capture 3 concrete follow-ups with owners and due dates.

Quick metrics snapshot (last 7d; pull from console before meeting if possible):
- Hosted API: avg tokens/sec per host: 420; p95 latency (text.generate): 210 ms; error rate 0.12% (spike 0.9% on 2026-03-08 during a rollout).
- Dedicated: 98% capacity utilization on GPU pools tagged wave-5; queue growth during prime hours +15% vs baseline.
- Private candidate trials: 6 active evals; 2 stalled waiting on IAM/KMS integration.

Conversation starters / prompts I want to use:
- "What are the one-minute risks that keep you up w.r.t wave-6 Dedicated?" (force out risk hierarchy)
- "If we need to delay wave-6 by one week, what is the minimal set of ship items we still cut?" (scope/rollback plan)
- "Can we reduce p95 by 20ms via kernel selection tweaks without impacting cost-more-than-2%?" (tradeoff call)

Open technical questions to surface (ask Marcus to confirm ownership):
1) Canary bucket config: do we need geo-split or customer-hash split? Tradeoffs: geo improves region-specific SLOs; hash gives even traffic sample. Current default: geo.
2) KV persistence: enabling persistent prefix cache for hosted reduces compute but increases storage and cold-start complexity. What is the real ops burden for persistence during resizes?
3) Private onboarding: which of these are blocking: VPC peering templates, KMS creds exchange flow, or smoke test automation? We need a single blocking checklist.

Proposed decisions (bring to meeting as options):
- Canary split: default to customer-hash for wave-6 (simpler sampling) unless SRE says geo is required for region-specific fallback tests.
- KV persistence: ship opt-in in wave-6; default enable target for wave-7 after 2 customer trials.
- Private onboarding: require full KMS integration before GA; allow early trials with "no-data" smoke tests.

Notes-to-self / context to share quickly:
- Sales flagged an enterprise wanting Private in APAC within 30 days — need a realistic lead-time estimate.
- Recent SRE note: kernel selection change in runtime PR #312 caused a 0.08% spike in telemetry due to oom kills on older drivers. Confirm regression fixed in ci/driver-upgrade branch.
- Console UX: rollout page shows ambiguous status when canary is in-progress; UX team has a patch but needs backend canary hooks (github PR linked above).

Draft agenda (20m):
1) 3m quick sync on metrics & blockers (I pull console snapshot live)
2) 6m Dedicated wave-6 gating checklist walkthrough + quick risk vote
3) 6m Private onboarding blockers & lead-time estimate
4) 3m KV persistence discussion and decision options
5) 2m assign follow-ups and confirm owners/due dates

Risk register (to surface quickly)
- Risk A (High): Wave-6 autoscaler misconfig under peak leads to customer-facing 5xxs. Mitigation: short-lived throttle policy + guaranteed fallback to smaller model family. Action: Marcus to validate autoscaler playbook; owner: Marcus; due: 2026-03-14.
- Risk B (Medium): KMS exchange flow for Private customers requires legal review for export controls. Mitigation: surface to security + legal early; Action: Priya to loop Legal; owner: Priya; due: 2026-03-16.
- Risk C (Medium): Enabling KV persistence might increase datastore ops by 1.5x on resizes. Mitigation: run two load tests with resize scenarios; Action: Evan to run perf test; owner: Evan; due: 2026-03-15.

Follow-ups to propose in the meeting (I want confirmation and acceptance):
- A: Autoscaler playbook + runbook finalize — Marcus — Due 2026-03-14.
- B: KMS/legal sync + decision on gating — Priya — Due 2026-03-16.
- C: KV persistence perf resilience runs (resize/cold-start) — Evan — Due 2026-03-15.
- D (bonus): Console canary UX backend hook review & small PR to add canary-state API — assign to "Console owner" (TBD) — Due 2026-03-18.

If we get extra time (nice-to-have list):
- Quick audit of cost impact if we schedule model-family fallbacks by default for certain SLAs.
- Short list of 3 customers to seed KV persistence trials (I have names from AE notes) — ask Marcus if ops team can handle 1 extra trial.

My meeting conduct reminders (notes to self):
- Don't let convo derail into infra-only rabbit hole — bring it back to customer impact and launch gating.
- Use "vote" mechanism: each risk gets a 3-count vote (stop / proceed-but-monitor / proceed).
- Capture decision in meeting doc and paste back to product/console channel.

Post-meeting template (for quick copy/paste into Slack and meeting notes):
- TL;DR decisions: [one-line decisions]
- Open actions: [list owner - item - due date]
- Blockers escalated: [list]
- Next sync: [date/time]

Stale ideas to avoid repeating in this meeting:
- Deep dive on kernel micro-optimizations (schedule separate session with Serving Runtime); only take high-level impact and risk.
- Re-hash design that already landed in PR #312 unless regression surfaced.

Final quick checklist before leaving meeting:
- Confirm owners + due dates for the 3 mandatory actions.
- Get verbal OK from Marcus on the canary split default.
- If legal/KMS is blocking Private GA, get commitment from Priya to escalate to security org.

Scratchpile (things to paste into meeting notes if requested):
- Example autoscaler throttle policy snippet (short): "if queue > 100 and avg latency > target -> cap new inflight, drop batch size by 20% for 60s, spin up burst nodes tagged wave-6-burst".
- Minimal KV persistence test matrix: small resize, cold-start, eviction scenario, crash-recovery.

End of prep.

-- H.

(If meeting runs over: follow-up to self: schedule 30m postmortem on any divergent decision; add to calendar and invite Marcus + Priya + Evan)
